title: "Normalization"

term: "Normalization"

## Simple explanation

Normalization changes values into a more convenient scale or form. In
machine learning, the word can refer to preparing input features or to
normalizing activations inside a neural network; the exact method matters.

## Technical explanation

Feature normalization may rescale values, for example to a fixed interval
or to zero mean and unit variance. Neural-network methods such as
Batch Normalization and Layer Normalization normalize intermediate
activations using statistics over different axes and may include learned
scale and shift parameters.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Appropriate normalization can improve numerical conditioning, make
optimization more stable, and reduce sensitivity to feature scales. The
choice depends on the data, model architecture, and inference setting;
normalization parameters must be computed without leaking validation or
test information into training.

## How it works

Standard score normalization of a feature uses training-set mean $\mu$ and
standard deviation $\sigma$:

$$
z = \frac{x-\mu}{\sigma}
$$

Other methods use ranges, norms, or statistics across a batch or feature
dimensions. Training and inference must use consistent statistics where
the method requires stored estimates.

## Practical example

If a dataset has one feature measured in millimeters and another in
millions of dollars, standardizing both using training-set statistics can
prevent their raw scales from dominating an optimization procedure.

## Common misconceptions

- Normalization is not one single algorithm; specify which data or activations are normalized and how.
- Normalization does not remove the need for sound train/validation/test splits.
- Batch Normalization and Layer Normalization use different statistics and behave differently.
